reuse.why: Extends the existing getScheduledAmount helper and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, the same tolerance function transaction matching uses.

duplication.why: No new copies of the rule; the only redundancy is schedule-template.ts keeping its own op ternary (now isbetween || isapprox) around the helper instead of calling it unconditionally.

placement.why: The approximate worst case is a private helper next to getWorstCaseAmount in shared/schedules.ts, and callers just pass their operator.

scope.why: Focused on threading the operator to callers; updating the schedule list display cells to show the worst-case value goes slightly beyond planning but is consistent.

maintainability.why: A single definition with an explicit op argument is easy to own; the loose string type for op, the positional insertion before inverse, and forecast taking op from two sources are small rough edges.

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount (getWorstCaseApproxAmount) is used by preview, posting, action sync, forecast, API, template and balance; schedule-template.ts still pre-filters on op before calling it, which is redundant but not a second definition.
